channel.title: Europe AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of European political, economic and security developments

item.title: German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on
item.description: Exit polls show damaging losses for Merz's centre-right CDU party in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin.

item.title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
item.description: Moscow's mayor says 450 drones were downed during the overnight barrage, in which two people died.

item.title: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
item.description: Denmark and the US have reached an agreement after months of threats from Donald Trump to annex the territory.

item.title: Shots heard as police start moving migrants from Ceuta beaches
item.description: Police reportedly fired into the air on Friday morning as they struggled to contain crowds jostling to secure a place at the tented site.

item.title: Warm words on Canada's EU 'associate membership' but no guarantees
item.description: There is no certainty that the idea will ever get off the ground, let alone become a blueprint for other countries, writes the BBC's Katya Adler.

item.title: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after election loss
item.description: Left-wing opposition parties led by Magdalena Andersson look set to form the next government.

item.title: Rosenberg: Russia's elections will have few surprises, but for the Kremlin they matter
item.description: There is no doubt over the outcome of this vote, but for the Kremlin they are still an important moment.

item.title: Eight German state premiers back Merz amid speculation over future
item.description: Christian Democratic Union leadership throws its weight behind the chancellor ahead of two state elections this weekend.

item.title: Zelensky appoints new chief prosecutor after predecessor's corruption scandal
item.description: Former chief prosecutor Ruslan Kravchenko after searches of his offices by Ukrainian anti-corruption officials.

item.title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire
item.description: The state post service delivers pensions, medicine and letters to people just miles from the front.

item.title: Carney's new love-in with EU has everything to do with Trump
item.description: The Canadian PM is in Strasbourg this week seeking a "unique alliance" - and there is one clear catalyst.

item.title: Why a fresh wave of North Korean soldiers may fight in Russia's war in Ukraine
item.description: North Korea will continue to send its soldiers to fight in Russia's war, but only for as long as it is profitable to do so, writes the BBC's Quentin Sommerville.

item.title: Watch: Why a Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation
item.description: No casualties were reported after a Russian drone struck a train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials left the area.

item.title: Merz’s election nightmare continues
item.description: Two state elections pile more pressure on German Chancellor Friedrich Merz — raising fresh questions about his leadership and what a weaker Germany could mean for the rest of Europe. Zoya Sheftalovich and Nick Vinocur also look at the growing fear over Russian hybrid attacks, as EU foreign ministers meet on the sidelines of the […]

item.title: From waste to wealth: Europe’s textile opportunity
item.description: With textiles now firmly part of Europe’s circular economy agenda, the EU must seize the opportunity to turn textile waste from a liability into a strategic resource.

item.title: Why the far right lost: 11 lessons for Europe from Sweden’s election
item.description: POLITICO spoke to party leaders Magdalena Andersson and Ulf Kristersson — and leading analysts — to understand the far-right Sweden Democrats' fall in support, and what it means.

item.title: Russia’s secret plan to supercharge kamikaze drone production
item.description: Documents obtained by POLITICO show a Russian state company blueprint for increasing drone carbon fiber production as the Kremlin escalates air war over Europe.

item.title: EU wants ‘closest possible’ relationship with Canada, Costa tells POLITICO
item.description: The European Council president said the EU and Canada can work together on defense, AI and strengthening democracy.

item.title: EU budget needs taxes governments aren’t already raising, Costa says
item.description: The European Council president spoke to POLITICO after visiting 25 capitals, and urged EU governments to soften red lines to secure a budget deal.

item.title: Merz vows to stay on as chancellor despite ‘disaster’ in another German regional vote
item.description: The embattled chancellor’s conservative party suffered its worst result in postwar German history as the far-right AfD won its second regional election in two weeks.
